stories.headline: Christine Lagarde will quit the European Central Bank early
body: Christine Lagarde says she will step down as ECB president in March, nine months before her term ends.
She says the job's neutrality rules stop her speaking her mind on world affairs.
She announced it after the ECB held interest rates; she is tipped as a possible head of the World Economic Forum.
stories.joke: Most people quit to speak freely about their boss. Lagarde quit to speak freely about the world.
stories.vc: A leadership change at the ECB means uncertainty over eurozone rates next year, which moves the euro and bond markets.

stories.statLabel: days to reopen Hormuz under the plan
stories.headline: JD Vance's letter to Iran may be the last chance to avoid new war
body: US Vice-President JD Vance wrote to Iran's top security official offering to restart talks, after mainly Qatari mediation.
The plan asks Iran to make nuclear commitments, leading to the Strait of Hormuz reopening within seven days in return for sanctions relief.
A reply is expected soon, but Tehran is reluctant to give ground first.
stories.joke: Diplomacy by letter. Very old school. Very high stakes.
stories.vc: A Hormuz reopening would ease oil and shipping costs fast; India, a big oil importer, would feel it in fuel prices.

image.credit: Senator Vance Press Office / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: China puts its last top general into the Politburo
body: China's leaders promoted the only remaining general on the military commission to the Politburo, the party's top body.
They also adopted a resolution on party discipline and fighting corruption.
The four-day meeting comes about a year before Xi Jinping is expected to seek a fourth term.
stories.joke: Promotions at the top are rare in China. So are open applications.
stories.vc: Tighter party control usually means more state direction of tech and industry, a key risk for foreign investors.

stories.headline: Sensex jumps 905 points as FMCG and PSU banks rally
body: The Sensex rose 905 points, about 1.2%, and the Nifty gained 238 points to 22,936 on Thursday.
FMCG and state-run bank stocks led the rally; Adani Ports, Kotak Mahindra and Eternal were top gainers.
Trent, Tech Mahindra and HDFC Bank fell.
stories.joke: One day down 353, next day up 905. The Sensex has mood swings.
stories.vc: Broad rallies after a fall show buyers are still keen, supportive for the busy IPO pipeline after Jio's debut.

stories.headline: Bengaluru's Pixxel sets up a US arm to win government deals
body: Satellite imaging startup Pixxel has created Pixxel Federal to sell to US government agencies.
It already works with NASA and the National Reconnaissance Office, and plans an office near Washington, DC.
The Bengaluru company raised $100 million last month.
stories.joke: From Bengaluru traffic to orbit to Washington. Quite the commute.
stories.vc: US defence and government budgets are the biggest buyers of satellite data; a local arm makes an Indian startup eligible.

stories.headline: ED probes ₹4,940 crore in cross-border crypto transfers
body: The Enforcement Directorate is investigating crypto platforms Mudrex and Saber.money and DeFi protocol Instadapp for alleged forex-law breaches.
It searched three premises in Bengaluru and one in Madhya Pradesh on 27 October.
It is the agency's second such probe in recent months.
stories.joke: Crypto promised freedom from regulators. Regulators did not agree.
stories.vc: Every new probe adds to India's crypto regulatory risk, keeping big investors cautious about the sector.

stories.headline: DoorDash agrees to buy Instacart for $17 billion
body: DoorDash will buy rival Instacart for $17 billion, or $65 a share; both boards have approved it.
It combines DoorDash's lead in restaurant delivery with Instacart's grocery business.
Instacart's CEO says the deal will help grocers of all sizes compete.
stories.joke: Your burrito and your broccoli, now from the same app.
stories.vc: Delivery consolidation shows scale wins; regulators will likely look closely, as with Zomato–Blinkit in India.

stories.headline: Amazon's cloud booms but AI spending burns its cash
body: Amazon missed forecasts for revenue and earnings, though its AWS cloud grew 39%.
Free cash flow over 12 months fell to minus $42.4 billion, from plus $14.8 billion a year earlier.
The spending is driven mainly by investment in AI.
stories.joke: Amazon: delivering everything, including a $42 billion cash hole.
stories.vc: Investors are starting to ask when the giant AI build-out pays back; that question shapes every AI valuation.

stories.headline: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings buys home security firm ADT
body: Thrive Holdings, a spinout of Josh Kushner's Thrive Capital, is buying ADT for about $7.6 billion in equity, $15.3 billion including debt.
OpenAI is a partner and investor, supplying models and engineers to Thrive's companies.
Thrive owns over 75 companies and aims to revamp them with AI.
stories.joke: Step one: buy a burglar alarm company. Step two: give it ChatGPT.
stories.vc: 'Buy old businesses and add AI' is a new private equity playbook; if it works, expect many copycats.

stories.headline: Reddit will put more content behind a login
body: Reddit says it is moving to a mainly logged-in experience as Google search traffic dries up.
It aims to protect its posts from AI scraping and sell data-licensing deals to AI labs.
Global daily users were flat last quarter and fell in the US.
stories.joke: Reddit to AI companies: the free buffet is closed.
stories.vc: User-made content is becoming a paid input for AI, a revenue line investors now value in social platforms.

stories.headline: Wabi, an AI agent that builds mini apps, hits a $1.25B valuation
body: Wabi raised $55 million at a $1.25 billion valuation.
It was founded by Eugenia Kuyda, who earlier started AI companion app Replika.
It now pitches itself as a personal agent that builds small apps for tasks like meal planning.
stories.joke: Why download an app when your AI can make one for you?
stories.vc: Investors are spreading bets across many AI assistants; few will win the 'one app' role.

stories.statLabel: Black women in the US Senate
stories.headline: Black women could double their seats in the US Senate
body: Only two Black women have ever served in the US Senate at the same time.
After Tuesday's election there will likely be three, possibly four, with Juliana Stratton and Angie Nixon running.
Since 1789, only about one in 400 US senators has been a Black woman.
stories.joke: Taking 237 years to reach four is not a speed record.
stories.vc: More diverse lawmakers tend to push on issues like childcare and maternal health, which shape the care economy.

stories.headline: Threats are driving women out of politics, rights group warns
body: Madison's mayor, Satya Rhodes-Conway, dropped her re-election bid on 23 October, citing threats to her safety.
Human Rights Watch says women in public life face high levels of violence, including online sexual abuse.
Women face more gendered and sexual attacks than men, it says, with little protection.
stories.vc: When women leave politics, policy on care, health and pay gaps loses champions; safety is now a cost of public life.

stories.headline: Azerbaijan's school dress rules shut out girls in hijabs
body: Schools in Azerbaijan began turning away girls wearing hijabs after new uniform rules took effect on 12 October.
The rules ban clothing 'inconsistent with secular education', without naming hijabs.
Protests followed, and police have detained dozens of people.
stories.vc: Keeping girls out of school cuts future earnings and growth; girls' education is one of development's highest-return investments.
